conventions.convention: A finite Coxeter matrix means S is finite; W need not be finite. An infinite off-diagonal label imposes no braid relation. The Artin presentations impose braid relations without generator-square relations.

The geometric type-A braid identification assumes AC and consumes the independently proved presentation-completeness theorem; the presentation constructions and positive-section arguments are choice-free.
Type-A permutations use the increasing relabelling k ↦ k+1 from {0,…,n−1} to {1,…,n}; products act with the rightmost factor first.
T_s²=(v_s−v_s⁻¹)T_s+1; S_s=v_sT_s and Q_s=v_s²; H_s=−T_s; T_s^EW=−v_s⁻¹T_s. In the original Kazhdan–Lusztig normalization the parameter is v⁻², whereas the S=qT example sets q=v.
Reflection faithfulness requires a faithful action and a bijection from reflections to their full codimension-one fixed spaces. Faithfulness of the canonical representation alone does not imply this.

K=2B, with unit simple-root norms. E_c has diagonal 1, entries K(e_si,e_sj) below the diagonal and zero above it; ω_c=E_c−E_cᵀ. Thus an earlier noncommuting simple root has positive ω-value against a later one.

Sorting words are lexicographically earliest increasing position sets in c∞. The greedy scan selects left descents of its remainder. Rank-two final subsequences are read inward from the other endpoint, in reverse angular order.
The sortable constructions assume finite type, meaning W is finite. Right weak order uses reduced prefixes and N(w⁻¹); w_J is the parabolic prefix in w=w_Jd, not the minimal coset representative d.

A skip is the first unselected occurrence of its simple generator. It is forced exactly when appending that generator to the selected prefix is nonreduced; its skip root is then negative. Cone inequalities are B(x,C_c^r(v))≥0, using the finite-type identification V≅V* by B.

⟨s⟩ denotes S minus {s} in the projection recursion. For initial s, sc deletes s, while scs rotates it to the end; recursive calls decrease the lexicographic pair (rank,length), with π_c(1)=1 including rank zero.

load_bearing.statement: For finite-type (W,S), a Coxeter element c, and a reduced word a₁⋯a_k for w with reflection roots β_i, ω_c(β_i,β_j)≥0 for all i≤j, strictly unless the reflections commute, iff w is c-sortable and the word converts to a c-sorting word by adjacent commuting transpositions. Also sortable iff aligned; sortable parabolic prefixes remain sortable for the restricted Coxeter element.

For finite-type (W,S), N(w_J⁻¹)=N(w⁻¹)∩Φ_J,+; w_J is the greatest W_J element below w, and the prefix map preserves meets and joins. For J=S minus {s}, if e_s is a cover root of w and every other cover reflection lies in W_J, then w=s∨w_J. If y∈W_J, cov(s∨y)=cov(y)∪{e_s}.

In finite type, a finite I⊆Φ_+ equals N(w) for some w iff its intersection with every noncommutative generalized rank-two positive system is empty, an initial segment, or a final segment. A sequence of distinct reflections is a reduced-word reflection sequence iff every generalized rank-two subsequence is endpoint-inward initial or final.

For finite-type (W,S), c a Coxeter element and v c-sortable, C_c(v) is a word-independent basis, and its negative roots are exactly −β_t for cover reflections t of v. If s is final in c and v≥_R s, then s is a cover reflection and v=s∨v_⟨s⟩. The same join decomposition holds for initial s when s is a cover reflection of v.

In finite type, π_c is order preserving and π_c(w) is the unique greatest c-sortable element below w. For every c-sortable v and every w, π_c(w)=v iff wC⊆Cone_c(v). For every J⊆S, π_c|J(w_J)=π_c(w)_J.

For a finite Coxeter matrix, assignments to a monoid or group satisfying every braid pair extend uniquely from A⁺ or A respectively. The generator assignment gives a surjection π:A→W and π∘γ=π⁺. If D is the normal closure of the generator squares in A, the induced A/D→W is an isomorphism and ker π=D.

For a finite Coxeter matrix, the reduced positive lift b_w∈A⁺ is expression-independent, b₁=[ε], and π⁺(b_w)=w; b is injective. The additive positive length satisfies L(b_w)=ℓ(w), and b_ub_v=b_uv iff ℓ(uv)=ℓ(u)+ℓ(v). If S is nonempty, neither b nor γ∘b is a homomorphism of the stated monoid/group.

The Hecke braid relations give a unique monoid map Θ:A⁺→H with Θ(σ_s)=T_s and Θ(b_w)=T_w. The four displayed unit-scaled quadratic presentations are isomorphic. If dim rad(B)=dim V−1≥1, the faithful canonical realization is not reflection faithful: distinct simple reflections have the same fixed hyperplane rad(B).

concerns.concern: The title says “Omega-positive reflection sequences are exactly the sorting words,” whereas Statement (1)(ii) correctly requires a word commutation-equivalent to a sorting word of a sortable element. In A₁×A₁ with c=st, the reduced word ts satisfies all zero-ω inequalities but the fixed-c sorting word is st. The title should retain the commuting-transposition qualification; the Statement and proof already do.

Proof 2.4 writes π_sc(w_⟨s⟩)≤_R w_⟨s⟩≤_R w “with equality if and only if w_⟨s⟩ is sc-sortable.” This qualification applies only to the first inequality. For A₂, c=st and w=ts, the prefix is t and is sortable, but π_c(w)=t<ts. The paragraph's final sentence supplies the correct additional condition w_⟨s⟩=w; clarify the earlier equality antecedent.

seams_checked.note: Reduced-lift proof uses Matsumoto braid connectivity for finite S without assuming finite W; exchange and type-A length clauses retain their stated conventions.
Canonical faithfulness is used without definiteness assumptions. The radical counterexample distinguishes it explicitly from reflection faithfulness.
The prerequisite closure uses the standard-parabolic presentation, support and length interfaces; no reflection-subgroup converse or stronger double-coset assertion is imported.
The seam lemma quotes T_w reduced-product independence, the R-basis theorem and arbitrary-ring base change exactly. Parameters remain constant on odd components, and S_s=v_sT_s with Q_s=v_s².
Uses right weak order through N(w⁻¹), simple-generator covers and left translation with the required descent conditions. Lattice and longest-element uses are restricted to finite type.
Root-plane stabilizers and chamber tiling retain finite type and positive-definite B. Cone statements use closed chambers; strict root signs are taken on interiors and extended by closure.

The three downstream theory items preserve finite type, greatest-sortable-below, monotonicity, parabolic compatibility, alignment and cover-decomposition hypotheses. Lattice-homomorphism and interval-fiber conclusions receive separate downstream arguments.
